article_title: 5cardsgame, innovative comprehensive integrative puzzle to enhance clinical reasoning in surgical technologist students: a pre-experimental study.
citation: Sadati Leila, Edalattalab Fatemeh, Abjar Rana, Karami Sahar, Hajati Niloofar. (2025). 5cardsgame, innovative comprehensive integrative puzzle to enhance clinical reasoning in surgical technologist students: a pre-experimental study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07057-2
title: 5CardsGame: a gamified modified Comprehensive Integrative Puzzle with five color-coded card sets for surgical procedures
description: The 5CardsGame is a modified Comprehensive Integrative Puzzle (CIP) built on script theory and gamification principles to assess and improve clinical reasoning. A panel selected five surgical procedures, and for each, five sets of color-coded cards were created: "Green: Preoperative care. Pink: Anatomy and surgical technique. White: Intraoperative care and instruments. Purple: Postoperative care. Yellow: Surgical complications." Players arrange five cards per scenario like puzzle pieces; points are awarded based on accuracy and speed with immediate feedback after each round.
requirements: Participants must have completed courses on principles and techniques of circular and scrub nursing, surgical technology, and operating room tools and equipment
An expert-validated checklist scoring accuracy (0 to 5 points per scenario) and completion time is needed for evaluation
constraints: The game covers five surgical procedures and, per the authors, "may not encompass all the complexities and variations encountered in real-world surgical settings"
target_learning_goals: integration of preoperative, anatomical, intraoperative, postoperative and complication knowledge into surgical procedure scripts
examples: In each round, six students participated simultaneously and arranged five cards per scenario stuck on the table, over a six-week period with three biweekly assessments

article_title: Use of situational judgment test for evaluating nonacademic attributes in ophthalmology fellowship selection.
citation: Prakasam Ruby Kala, Tripathi Anjali, Kapoor Aditya, Bejjanki Kavya M, Pathengay Avinash, Snigdha Snigdha. (2026). Use of situational judgment test for evaluating nonacademic attributes in ophthalmology fellowship selection. Indian Journal of Ophthalmology. https://doi.org/10.4103/IJO.IJO_2484_25
title: Verbal construct-driven SJT with 5Cs rubric and real-time scoring
description: A verbal situational judgment test in which interviewers present clinical or professional scenarios and grade responses in real time against a predefined rubric based on the 5Cs framework: communication, collaboration, critical thinking, curiosity, and creativity, plus overall grooming and interview preparedness. Unlike traditional SJT methodologies involving post-hoc transcription and coding, "Participants verbalized their reasoning during the interview, and responses were evaluated immediately using a standardized rubric based on the 5C framework." Each response option represents a different approach with a weighted percentage score, and there was no single correct answer.
requirements: Scenario and rubric development with iterative revision based on panel feedback
Real-time scoring by a trained evaluator
constraints: Administered online, which the authors note may have affected candidate performance through technical challenges and reduced interpersonal interaction
target_learning_goals: assessing nonacademic attributes: communication, collaboration, critical thinking, curiosity, creativity
examples: One collaboration scenario asks candidates how they would handle team members favoring another approach in a patient awareness campaign brainstorm
